summary:
Martian Map is an app that helps astronauts plan a safe walk on Mars. We chose Jezero Crater, where NASA's Perseverance rover works. There, a river once flowed into a lake. The rocks may keep signs of old life.

The app shows NASA maps one on top of the other: photos from space, a height map, a heat map and a rock map. The team picks the places to visit, and the app draws a safe path. The path goes around steep hills, big rocks and soft sand. The app also shows the walking time, the oxygen left, the time of day on Mars, the cold and the air pressure. It warns the team when something is not safe.

This is important because on Mars, astronauts have little oxygen, it is very cold, and the ground is new to them.
details:
What it does

Martian Map helps two astronauts and their rover plan a walk on Mars. It has two screens:

- *Planning screen:* the team turns maps on and off and clicks on the map to add stops. The app finds the safest path. It does not go on slopes over 15° or through big rocks, and it avoids soft sand. It shows the distance, the climb, the walking time and the oxygen left. Each stop has a card with the task, a photo from Perseverance, the time of arrival, the cold and the air pressure.

- *Helmet screen:* a simple screen for walking. It shows which way to go, the next stop, how far it is, how steep it is, the time, the cold, the oxygen left and the time to go back to the rover.

Safety

The app warns the team when:

- the walk is longer than the oxygen;

- the walk ends after dark;

- it is very cold;

- the ground is too steep or sandy.

The astronauts always walk in pairs, and the rover follows them.

NASA data we used

- Mars Trek: photos from space, height map, heat map

- USGS-NASA: rock map

- Curiosity route video: idea for drawing the path

- NASA Worldview: idea for the app design

- Perseverance photos: what you see at each stop

- Perseverance weather data: about −83 °C to −22 °C, very thin air (about 718 Pa)

Tools we used

HTML, CSS and JavaScript, so the app works on any device, even without internet. A smart method called A* finds the safest path. Python makes the paper map. No special hardware is needed.

Who it helps

- Astronauts: safer walks and more time to work.

- NASA teams: plan and test a walk before going to Mars.

- Scientists: reach the best rocks in time.

- The Moon and Earth: the same idea can help on the Moon, and rescue teams in deserts or mountains.

- Students: an easy way to learn with real NASA data.

Why it is creative

It puts the map, the path, the time, the weather and safety in one simple tool. The helmet screen shows only the most important facts, so the astronaut can stay focused.

What we thought about

- Safety first: oxygen, slopes, rocks, sand, cold, daylight and the way back.

- A helmet screen that is easy to read, even when the astronaut is tired.

- Being honest: our map is a simple model of Jezero. Real Mars Trek images can be added to the app. Warnings for sun storms will come in a later version.
